title: New Grafana dashboard 08_accuracy_cost.json rendering the WI-1 headline question
description: Build etl4/dashboard/08_accuracy_cost.json (uid etl4-accuracy-cost, title 'ETL4 - Accuracy vs Cost (WI-1)') with 9 panels: hero markdown; Pareto scatter from v_pareto_frontier; metric heatmap table from fact_experiment_result (seg_f1 with continuity fallback); throughput/latency/memory scale curves from scale_runs; skip-and-log evidence table; metric completeness bargauge from eval_results; reviewer explainer markdown. All queries use the Postgres datasource (uid Postgres). Panels render gracefully on empty data pre-T-003.
acceptance_criteria: python -c 'import json; d=json.load(open(path)); print(len(d["panels"]), d["uid"])' prints 9 etl4-accuracy-cost
Grafana API /api/search lists uid etl4-accuracy-cost in the ETL4 folder within 32 seconds of file write
Grafana API /api/dashboards/uid/etl4-accuracy-cost returns the 9-panel JSON without error
Every rawSql parses in Postgres via docker exec psql with exit 0 (may return 0 rows pre-T-003 matrix rerun)
No em-dash, right-arrow, or non-cp1252 characters in dashboard JSON (fancy quotes or ASCII arrows -> '-' / 'to')
Default time range is absolute wide window '2026-01-01' to 'now'
Title 'ETL4 - Accuracy vs Cost (WI-1)' and tags ['etl4','wi-1','pareto','accuracy-cost','scale']
contract_deviations: Metric completeness panel: task text says 'stat panel tile row ... One stat per metric'. Implemented as a single bargauge panel ranging over the 6 metric names rather than 6 separate stat panels so the total dashboard panel count stays in the stated 8-10 range (9 panels total). The bargauge still shows one tile per metric with populated vs total_cells, matching the intent. Resolution: applied-per-intent, panel-count-constraint.

Panel 8 queries eval_results rather than fact_experiment_result. The fact_experiment_result mart only has rmse_m and seg_f1 columns; the other four metrics (seg_precision, seg_recall, coverage_ratio, boundary_err_s) land in eval_results via sink/postgres.py::_PERSISTED_METRICS. Querying eval_results is the correct source for 'how many cells have non-NULL values per metric'. Verified via distinct metric scan of eval_results (9 metric names present). Resolution: applied-per-data-shape.
